P1.fact: 5.Nxf7: the knight on e5 takes the pawn on f7.
The knight on f7 attacks the queen on g5.
The knight on f7 attacks the rook on h8.
Black's queen on g5 already attacks White's pawn on g2.
After 5.Nxf7 nothing defends the pawn on g2.
5...Qxg2: Black's queen on g5 takes the pawn on g2.
The queen on g2 attacks the rook on h1.
White could have played 5.Bxf7+ instead of 5.Nxf7.
5.Bxf7+: White's bishop on c4 takes the pawn on f7.
The bishop on f7 gives check to the king on e8.
The bishop on f7 attacks the knight on g8.
After 5.Bxf7+, Black must answer the check, so the queen on g5 cannot play 5...Qxg2 at once.

P2.fact: 7.Be2: the bishop on c4 goes back from c4 to e2.
The bishop on e2 blocks the check from the queen on e4.
7.Be2 was not the only way to block the check: 7.Qe2 also blocks it.
Black's king on e8 already attacks White's knight on f7.
After 7.Be2 nothing defends the knight on f7.
Black's queen on e4 pins the bishop on e2 to the king on e1.
7...Nf3#: Black's knight on d4 goes forward from d4 to f3.
7...Nf3# gives check to the king on e1, and it is mate: the game ends, and Black wins.
The bishop on e2 cannot take the knight on f3: the queen on e4 pins it to the king on e1.
White could have played 7.Qe2 instead of 7.Be2.
7.Qe2: White's queen on d1 goes forward from d1 to e2.
The queen on e2 blocks the check from the queen on e4.
The queen on e2 attacks the queen on e4.
The queen on e2 defends the bishop on c4.
The queen on e2 pins the queen on e4 to the king on e8.

P3.fact: 1.h3: the pawn on h2 goes forward from h2 to h3.
Now the king on g1 can step to h2.
Black's king on g8 is shut in by its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7.
White could have played 1.Rd8# instead of 1.h3.
1.Rd8#: White's rook on d1 goes forward from d1 to d8.
1.Rd8# gives check to the king on g8, and it is mate: the game ends, and White wins.

P4.fact: 1.Kd2: the king on e1 steps forward from e1 to d2.
White could have played 1.Nc7+ instead of 1.Kd2.
1.Nc7+: White's knight on d5 goes forward from d5 to c7.
The knight on c7 gives check to the king on e8.
The knight on c7 attacks the rook on a8.
1.Nc7+ gives check; after the king moves, the knight on c7 takes the rook on a8 (2.Nxa8).

P5.fact: 1.e3: the pawn on e2 goes forward from e2 to e3.
1.e3 frees the queen on d1: it could not move before.
1.e3 frees the bishop on f1: it could not move before.
The bishop on c1 was already shut in by the pawns on b2 and d2 before 1.e3, and 1.e3 does not free it.
White could have played 1.d4 instead of 1.e3.
1.d4: White's pawn on d2 goes forward from d2 to d4.

H1.fact: 4.d3: the pawn on d2 goes forward from d2 to d3.
The pawn on d3 defends the bishop on c4.
4.d3 frees the bishop on c1: it could not move before.
Black's knight on f6 already attacks White's queen on h5.
After 4.d3 nothing defends the queen on h5.
White could have played 4.Qxf7# instead of 4.d3.
4.Qxf7#: White's queen on h5 takes the pawn on f7.
4.Qxf7# gives check to the king on e8, and it is mate: the game ends, and White wins.

H2.fact: 1.Kf2+: the king on g1 steps forward from g1 to f2.
The bishop on g2 gives check to the king on d5.
White could have played 1.Bf3+ instead of 1.Kf2+.
1.Bf3+: White's bishop on g2 goes forward from g2 to f3.
The bishop on f3 gives check to the king on d5.
1.Bf3+ gives check; after the king moves, the bishop on f3 takes the rook on b7 (2.Bxb7).

H3.fact: 1.Qf7: the queen on f1 goes forward from f1 to f7.
1.Qf7 is stalemate: Black has no legal move and is not in check, so the game ends at once as a draw.
White could have played 1.Qf8# instead of 1.Qf7.
1.Qf8#: White's queen on f1 goes forward from f1 to f8.
1.Qf8# gives check to the king on h8, and it is mate: the game ends, and White wins.

H4.fact: 1.Kg2: the king on g1 steps forward from g1 to g2.
Black's knight on e5 cannot move, because the rook on e1 pins it to the king on e8.
White could have played 1.f4 instead of 1.Kg2.
1.f4: White's pawn on f2 goes forward from f2 to f4.
The pawn on f4 attacks the knight on e5.

H5.fact: 1.Qc1: the queen on d1 goes sideways from d1 to c1.
1...Ne2+: Black's knight on d4 goes forward from d4 to e2.
The knight on e2 gives check to the king on g1.
The knight on e2 attacks the queen on c1.
1...Ne2+ gives check; after the king moves, the knight on e2 takes the queen on c1 (2...Nxc1).
White could have played 1.Qxd4 instead of 1.Qc1.
1.Qxd4: White's queen on d1 takes the knight on d4.
